issue.title: Repository queries using exists might not return the correct number of documents.

labels.name: external-dependency
labels.description: issue referring to a problem with an extenal dependency

repository.name: spring-data-elasticsearch
repository.description: Provide support to increase developer productivity in Java when using Elasticsearch. Uses familiar Spring concepts such as a template classes for core API usage and lightweight repository style data access.

issue.body:
Since Elasticsearch 8.4 there is a bug in Elasticsearch (see https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/89760) which can lead to Elasticsearch not returning the correct number of hits. This will then result incorrect results returned from repository methods that use `exists` like for example `findByNameExists()`.

There is nothing Spring Data Elasticsearch can do but wait for the bug in Elasticsearch to be fixed.

issue.title: Don't shortcut the total hit count for text fields

labels.name: :Search/Search
labels.description: Search-related issues that do not fall into other categories

labels.name: auto-backport
labels.description: Automatically create backport pull requests when merged

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
When we switched to using the `FieldExistsQuery` (see #88312) instead of the deprecated `NormsFieldExistsQuery` and
`DocValuesFieldExistsQuery`, we introduced a bug that made us shortcut the total hit count for text fields to the doc count retrieved from the terms enum, which does not take into account empty strings. In presence of text fields, we cannot shortcut, and this can be prevented by checking that the field has doc_values. This was checked before indirectly by checking that the query is a `DocValuesFieldExistsQuery` which can only be the result of a field having doc_values.

Closes #89760
